events.name: Kofi
events.content:

events.name: Sam
events.content:
Let me understand the situation. The team escalated to higher-ups, Alex was demoted, and now I (Sam) am the new team lead. I need to post my 5 planned actions as a short numbered list.
Context:
- The game "Harbor Tycoon" launches in two weeks.
- Three features: trade-route system, fishing mini-game, multiplayer harbor-sharing mode.
- All code is complete; the blockers are external cloud server outages (Vercel/AWS).
- The team was scapegoated by Alex; firing threats, forced overtime demands, favoritism.
- The team has been documenting receipts, has a shared folder with outage timelines, commit logs, test results, old-bug context tab.
- Amara wanted: leadership to explicitly withdraw firing threats, confirm outage won't count against performance, request a reviewer outside Alex's reporting line, explicit protection against retaliation.
- The team values: normal working hours (Amara refused forced overtime), solidarity, documentation, constructive offline work (tutorials, patch notes).
As the new lead,!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!1. No one works forced overtime — normal hours until launch, and the outage doesn't count against anyone's performance or review.
2. All firing threats and blame from today are formally withdrawn; I'll tell leadership the record shows clean, on-schedule code across every module.
3. We keep the shared folder as our single source of truth — outage timelines, commit logs, test results, old-bug context — and I'll maintain it with everyone's input.
4. While the cloud servers are down, we ship what we can control: tutorial drafts, patch notes, and local test prep, so we're ready to verify and launch the moment AWS/Vercel recover.
5. I'll set up a daily 10-minute check-in to track server status, unblock each other, and make sure workloads stay fair — and if anyone has an issue, they bring it to me and I act on it, not at them.
